notes:
Account snapshot and POC specifics:
- Company: mid-market SaaS (product analytics) building an in-product assistant + context-aware support workflows. Heavy use of embeddings for doc search and a reranking pipeline for in-app suggestions.
- Decision path: evaluating hosted API first (took demo), now moving to Dedicated POC to validate throughput and VPC constraints. Primary driver: predictable latency for in-app assistant and isolation for customer data.
- POC ask (agreed): 2-week Dedicated canary in their staging VPC. Scope: 3 model endpoints (chat assistant, 1536-dim embeddings, reranker). Load profile: steady 10 qps for chat with 95th percentile latency target < 250ms; embeddings burst to 20 qps.
- Canary plan (agreed with SE):
  * Week 0 (setup): VPC peering, credentials, SSO test account, baseline metrics collection
  * Week 1 (canary): Route 5-10% of internal staging traffic to Dedicated canary (controlled split). Measure latency, token cost, error rates, mem utilization.
  * Week 2 (stress/validation): Gradually increase traffic to 30% then back to 0% for rollback validation. Verify autoscaling behavior and burst capacity.
- Fallback & rollback policy (documented in SOW):
  * Primary route: Dedicated pool in us-west (customer preferred region).
  * Model variants: default production model (fp16/quantized variant enabled), fallback to cheaper 8-bit quantized variant when cost pressure triggered or capacity constrained. Also fallback to hosted API as an emergency safety net with traffic shaping.
  * Region failover: if us-west Dedicated pool has sustained errors or degradation >5% in SLOs for 10m, automatic routing to us-east Dedicated pool (if available) otherwise to hosted API in us-west.
  * Rollback: immediate rollback to hosted API route and pause canary if error spike >3x baseline error rate or latency >500ms for 95th for 5m.
- Success metrics for POC: 95th p99 latency < 300ms for chat (target 250ms), cost per 1k tokens within 25% of modeled Dedicated estimate, zero data leakage incidents, SAML SSO passes security test.
- Security notes: security team cares about audit log samples, KMS key residency, and retention controls. Provided security FAQ doc (linked). Customer asked for sample audit logs from a similar POC — SE to prepare redacted sample.
- Pricing conversation: mid-market reserved monthly commit vs on-demand tradeoffs. Customer wants a predictable monthly cap with burst credits. Pricing gap vs incumbent (existing vendor) ~15% on list price; open to committed discount if 12mo commit.
- Quotes & docs: SOW draft v1 shared on 2026-03-01 (Drive link). SE to update SOW with canary rollback matrix and routing diagrams.
- Quotes from customer: "We need to prove stable latency under realistic in-app traffic before we can move to procurement." - Head of Product.
- Risks: network egress path for VPC peering still unvalidated (blocker), legal wants data residency clarity for EU customers (we're NA HQ but EU customers exist), security asks may add 2 weeks.
- Next actions (short): Finish SOW edits (SE), send revised pricing scenarios (AE), schedule infra kickoff 03/15, provide redacted audit log sample by 03/12.
